title: GPU particles clump up when emitted at higher speed
body:
### Tested versions

v4.3.stable.official [77dcf97d8]

### System information

Godot v4.3.stable - Windows 10.0.19045 - Vulkan (Mobile) - dedicated AMD FirePro W2100 (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 27.20.21026.2006) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-7600 CPU @ 3.50GHz (4 Threads)

### Issue description

I'm trying to implement an after burner for a space ship.  This is basically a particle stream that shoots straight and tapers over time.  The particle stream being emitted is anything but smooth, even thought I do not see any reason why it should not be.

I started a discussion about this here: https://forum.godotengine.org/t/why-is-gpuparticles3d-initial-velocity-causing-my-particle-flame-to-hop/97319/3

### Steps to reproduce

Run the attached project.  Alternately, create a GPUParticles3D and set the number to 400, the lifetime to .1.  Create a ParticleProcessMaterial and the linear velocity to 15.  

I would expect this to create a smooth stream of particles that bend smoothly when I move the thruster object from side to side in the Godot editor and when I run it in the the game.  Instead, the flame hops back and forth.  I can stop the hopping by unchecking Interpolation, but nothing I can do stops the particles from forming little line segments when I move the thruster object in the scene. 

If you run the project, you will see one of the thrusters who's object is stationary, but which none the less appears to hop back and forth due to some sort of clumping of the particles.  There is a second thruster that moves around due to an AnimationPlayer.  You can see the particle stream project into several chunks instead of animating smoothly.

I would expect the particles to be independent and the flame to both be emitted smoothly and sway gracefully as the thruster object is moved around.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[clumpy-particle-fire.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18358801/clumpy-particle-fire.zip)
